name: Autosomal Dominant Spastic Paraplegia Type 41

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Dominant Spastic Paraplegia

criteria.description: Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Pathogenic mutation in the ATP13A2 gene confirmed by genetic testing
Exclusion of other causes of spastic paraplegia by clinical and laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive lower limb spasticity with a positive family history and confirmed pathogenic ATP13A2 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation may vary in severity.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Degeneration of the lateral corticospinal tracts

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic and inflammatory causes
imaging: MRI brain and spinal cord may show mild corticospinal tract degeneration
other: Electromyography may show mild chronic neurogenic changes
Nerve conduction studies typically normal or mildly abnormal

distinguishingFeatures: SPG7 typically presents with cerebellar ataxia and optic atrophy
Rapid progression with upper and lower motor neuron signs
Absence of family history in most cases

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks to months
Presence of lower motor neuron signs such as muscle atrophy and fasciculations
references: Orphanet: Autosomal Dominant Spastic Paraplegia Type 41 (ORPHA:320355)
Harding AE. Hereditary spastic paraplegias. Semin Neurol. 1993;13(4):333-342.
Bras J, Vermeer S, Schneider SA, et al. Mutations in ATP13A2 cause hereditary spastic paraplegia type 41. Brain. 2012;135(6):1810-1820.
